title: Partial visions of utilitarianism: A critical examination of the Oxford Utilitarianism Scale and CNI frameworks.
abstract: This study aimed to clarify the psychological structure of utilitarian moral judgment by examining how individual differences in, and an experimental manipulation of, utilitarian thinking relates to scores on the Oxford Utilitarianism Scale (OUS) and the CNI model. Study 1 (N = 312) examined the associations between personality variables and scores from the OUS and CNI models using correlational analyses. The results revealed that the Impartial Beneficence dimension of OUS was positively related with Light Triad traits, Prosocial Behavior, Religiosity, and negatively related with Machiavellianism. The N parameter of the CNI was found to be positively associated with Kantianism, Religiosity, Action-Oriented prosociality, and negatively associated with the Dark Triad traits, Instrumental Harm and Relativism, while the C parameter was only related to the I parameter. Additionally, Instrumental Harm showed positive associations with Dark Triad traits. In Study 2, participants in the experimental group (N = 80) read a text promoting utilitarianism, while those in the control condition (N = 86) read a neutral text. Subsequent changes in participants' OUS and CNI scores were examined. The findings indicated a significant increase in Impartial Beneficence scores, a significant decrease in C scores, and a significant decrease in N scores in the experimental group. Overall, the findings suggest that the CNI and OUS parameters capture different aspects of utilitarianism while also highlighting the potential for both approaches to be further developed to offer a more comprehensive understanding of utilitarian moral judgment.
